newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo port expects to handle 3.5 mln TEUs by 200.
newsitem.headline: Colombo port expects to handle 3.5 mln TEUs by 200.

text.p: Sri Lanka's main Colombo port expects to handle 2.1 million TEU (twenty-foot equivalent unit) containers by the year 2000 and 3.5 million TEUs by 2005, the Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA) said.
The SLPA's internal journal, seen by Reuters on Monday, forecast increasing demand for container handling and said steps were being taken to address the need.

The company magazine said South Asia Gateway Terminals Ltd (SAGT), a joint venture led by units of Britain's Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co -- P&O Navigation Australia, P&O containers, Sri Lankan conglomerate John Keells Holdings and the SLPA -- had been asked to develop the Queen Elizabeth Quay.
SAGT would expand the quay's container capacity to a million units a year from the current 250,000, and simultaneously start building a new port adjacent to the existing one.
The quay is currently part of Colombo port but is being leased and developed separately.
The new port, to be developed in phases, will eventually have 11 berths capable of handling four million containers a year and a deeper draft to handle the next generation of ships.

"The plans in Colombo will also be supplemented with a proposal to develop the (southern) port of Galle for which a letter of intent for build-operate-transfer (BOT) investment has been issued," the journal said.
It did not name the company which had received the letter of intent and did not give further details.
